scientific_name: Puccinia triticina (syn. P. recondita f. sp. tritici)
favorable_conditions: Temperature 15-25°C, relative humidity >60%, dew formation, southerly winds carrying spores from central India, mid-to-late season crop
economic_impact: 10-30% yield loss (up to 50% in susceptible varieties). Most common rust of wheat in India, occurs almost every year in Punjab, Haryana, UP.
symptoms: Small (1-2 mm) circular to oval orange-brown pustules (uredia) on upper leaf surface
Pustules scattered randomly on leaves — NOT in stripes (distinguishes from yellow rust)
Reddish-brown powdery spores released when pustule is rubbed
Late season: black telia develop as crop matures
Severe infection causes premature leaf drying and shrivelled grains

treatment.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt 25 EC) at 1ml/L water at first appearance of pustules. Spray in evening (4-6 PM) for best absorption. Repeat after 15 days if pustules reappear. 500ml per acre.
treatment.biological: No effective biological control available for cereal rusts.
treatment.cultural: Timely sowing (late October to mid-November in NW India). Avoid very late sowing. Balanced nitrogen fertilization. Report rust incidence to District Agriculture Officer.
treatment.dosage: 1ml per liter of water, 500ml per acre

source: ICAR-Indian Institute of Wheat and Barley Research (IIWBR), Karnal; PAU Ludhiana Rabi Advisory

favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (10-15°C), high humidity, cloud cover, early-sown wheat, December-February in North India, spores arrive from Nilgiri Hills
economic_impact: 25-70% yield loss if untreated. Most destructive wheat rust — can destroy an entire crop if left unchecked. Major threat to NW India wheat belt.
symptoms: Yellow-orange pustules arranged in LINEAR STRIPES along leaf veins — key diagnostic
Stripes can be several cm long on leaves and leaf sheaths
Yellow powdery spores released profusely when touched
Infected leaves turn yellow prematurely and dry from tip
Flag leaf infection severely reduces grain filling — shrivelled grains

treatment.chemical: IMMEDIATE spray of Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt) at 1ml/L water the moment yellow stripes are seen. Do NOT wait — this rust spreads fastest. Spray entire field including borders. Second spray after 15 days mandatory.
treatment.biological: No effective biological control for stripe rust.
treatment.cultural: Critical: Report to nearest Agriculture Department immediately — enables regional advisory. Use certified seed of resistant varieties. Avoid very early sowing before October 25. Destroy volunteer wheat plants.
treatment.dosage: 1ml per liter of water, 500ml per acre
treatment.alert: URGENT — spray immediately upon detection. Every day of delay increases yield loss significantly.

source: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal; Directorate of Wheat Research; PAU Regional Research Station, Flowerdale (Shimla)

favorable_conditions: Seed-borne disease — infection occurs at flowering of previous crop. Cool moist weather during flowering aids infection. Using farm-saved untreated seed perpetuates disease.
economic_impact: 1-5% yield loss normally, but can reach 20-40% if untreated seed used for multiple seasons. Completely destroys infected earheads.
symptoms: Entire earhead replaced by mass of dark brown/black spores (powdery mass)
Affected earheads emerge earlier than healthy ones — often first visible heads in field
Spores dispersed by wind, infecting nearby flowering healthy plants
After spore dispersal, only bare rachis (axis) remains
No external symptoms until heading — internally seed-borne

treatment.chemical: SEED TREATMENT (before sowing): Carboxin 75% WP (Vitavax) at 2g/kg seed, or Carbendazim 50% WP (Bavistin) at 2g/kg seed. Best: Carboxin + Thiram (Vitavax Power) at 2g/kg. No foliar spray is effective.
treatment.biological: Treat seed with Trichoderma viride at 4g/kg seed as bio-control agent.
treatment.cultural: Use certified disease-free seed. Rogue out smutted earheads before spore release (early morning when heads are still covered). Do not save seed from infected fields.
treatment.dosage: 2g per kg of seed — mix thoroughly before sowing

favorable_conditions: Cool temperatures (18-22°C), light rain/high humidity during heading-flowering stage, cloudy weather, thick crop canopy, high nitrogen
economic_impact: 1-4% grain infection normally, but gives FISHY ODOR to grain making it unmarketable. Quarantine pest — affected grain rejected in export markets.
symptoms: Partial conversion of wheat grain to black powdery mass (bunted grain)
Only part of the kernel is affected — usually one side (distinguishes from other bunts)
Fishy/rotten smell (trimethylamine) when infected grain is crushed — characteristic
When threshed, black spores dust healthy grains giving dark appearance
Symptoms visible only after harvest when grain is examined, or at heading in severe cases

treatment.chemical: Spray Propiconazole 25% EC at 1ml/L water at boot leaf/flag leaf stage (Zadoks 45-49) if weather conditions are conducive. Repeat at heading if rain continues. Seed treatment: Thiram 75% WP at 2.5g/kg seed.
treatment.biological: No effective biological control established for Karnal bunt.
treatment.cultural: Use certified Karnal bunt-free seed. Avoid late sowing. Do not use grain from infected lots for seed. Deep summer ploughing to bury teliospores.
treatment.recommended_pesticide: Propiconazole 25% EC (Tilt 25 EC) at boot stage
treatment.dosage: 1ml per liter of water at flag leaf/boot stage
treatment.spray_interval: One spray at boot stage, second at heading if needed

source: ICAR-IIWBR Karnal; National Bureau of Plant Genetic Resources (NBPGR)
